issues.issue: COMMIT semantics and route-swap ordering are defined three incompatible ways. connection_plane: COMMIT = a single atomic `route.store({authority:dest})` on the gateway, performed by the gateway when it receives `CommitAuthority` from the saga; the gateway swap IS the commit and the Directory records the flip only after the `Committed` ack. transfer_protocol: ordered Demote-before-Promote, where the *Coordinator* writes `version=N+1` to redb (the commit point), then waits source `DemoteAck`, then `Promote`, then a SEPARATE later `RouteSwap{client,dest}` message to the gateway after `CommitAck` — so the gateway swaps AFTER commit, in a distinct phase. identity_persistence: COMMIT = a CAS on `directory[E].fence`; the gateway/dest *derive* authority by reading the directory and the gateway 'forwards session S iff directory[session:S].authority==self' (no explicit RouteSwap command at all). These cannot all be true: the gateway either (a) swaps on an explicit command at commit (conn), (b) swaps on a separate post-promote command (transfer), or (c) polls/derives from the directory (identity).
issues.resolution: identity_persistence + transfer_protocol win on the durable commit point; connection_plane wins on the gateway mechanism. Unify to: COMMIT = a single linearizable directory CAS on the owner record's fence (the durable commit point, owned by the orchestrator/Coordinator). The gateway does NOT poll the directory on the data path (identity_persistence's 'forwards iff directory==self' is too slow for 20Hz and contradicts its own lock-free hot path). Instead the Coordinator, immediately after the winning CAS, sends connection_plane's `CommitAuthority`/RouteSwap to the gateway, which performs the single atomic `route.store`. Drop transfer_protocol's separate ROUTE_SWAP-as-its-own-phase; fold it into the post-CAS notification. Keep transfer_protocol's Demote-before-Promote ordering AND the gateway lease-epoch/fence frame-drop fence so a stale source cannot affect the client between CAS and the gateway store. Net pipeline: PrepareSubscribe/ghost -> RequestCut/freeze input boundary -> directory CAS(fence+1) [commit] -> notify gateway -> gateway atomic route.store -> Demote source -> Release.

issues.issue: Three overlapping authority-generation/fence mechanisms with different names, widths, and scopes. connection_plane: `session_gen:u32` (per-session fence on input/commands, CAS-bumped on gateway adoption) plus `RouteSnapshot`/`SeqCut`. transfer_protocol: `lease_epoch:u64` (++ on every owner change, the gateway frame-drop fence) AND `version:u64` (++ on every authority change, the CAS expected value) — two separate monotonic numbers per OwnerRecord. identity_persistence: a single `Fence(u64)` ('the ONLY linearizable fact about authority') used for BOTH entity ownership and session ownership, plus `gateway_gen` (session fence) and a mentioned `lease_version`. So the same linearizability primitive exists as {session_gen}, {lease_epoch+version}, and {Fence+gateway_gen+lease_version}. transfer_protocol's twin version-vs-lease_epoch is itself a latent inconsistency (two numbers that must move together).
issues.resolution: identity_persistence's unification wins as the principle (one fence primitive), but adopt transfer_protocol's explicit gateway-frame-drop semantics for it. Define ONE `Fence(u64)` per directory key, bumped on every ownership change, never reused, carried on every authoritative action and inter-process message; receivers reject `fence < highest_seen`. Collapse transfer_protocol's `version` and `lease_epoch` into this single fence (they were never independently needed — every owner change is an authority change). Session ownership uses the SAME fence type on a `session:<id>` key; rename connection_plane's `session_gen` to that fence (keep u64 not u32 to match). Delete `lease_version` as a separate concept. This makes the directory CAS, the gateway frame-drop, and the gateway-adoption fence the same mechanism — which is exactly each design's stated goal, just triplicated.

issues.issue: Two mutually-exclusive input-boundary ('cut') mechanisms. connection_plane: the client emits an in-band `CUT_MARKER` token on the unreliable INPUT datagram stream at `marker_seq` (client-authoritative); the gateway routes seq<=marker to source, seq>marker to dest buffer; correctness rests on the client emitting the marker on request and the durable seq-range interval map. transfer_protocol: there is NO client cut — the SOURCE shard freezes the entity, drains its bounded input ring, ships `input_backlog`+`last_tick` in `FlushComplete`, and a missing backlog surfaces as a typed `InputGap{from,to}` to the client. These are two different answers to 'where is the input timeline severed': client-emitted seq marker vs server-side freeze+flush+gap. They also imply different client obligations (emit CUT_MARKER vs nothing) and different gateway state (per-seq routing table vs none).
issues.resolution: connection_plane wins — it owns the wire and the gateway route table, and the client-emitted CUT_MARKER on the ordered-by-seq input stream is the only mechanism that severs the input timeline with zero cross-stream race (the freeze-flush-backlog model re-introduces a server-side input buffer whose loss becomes the InputGap, i.e. exactly the stale-state artifact connection_plane's datagram design avoids). transfer_protocol must change: FreezeSource consumes input only up to the gateway-confirmed `marker_seq` (not a self-chosen freeze instant); there is no source-side input ring to flush and no `input_backlog` field; dest applies gateway-buffered post-marker frames after commit. transfer_protocol's `InputGap` becomes the rare-failure-only signal (forced resolution when the marker was never confirmed), not the normal path. The client MUST emit CUT_MARKER on `RequestCut` — add that obligation to identity_persistence/test_harness client models too.

issues.issue: Coordinate-frame authority is modeled three ways. connection_plane: server sends `ReferenceFrameDef{frame_id, orbital_elements|rigid, validity_range}` on CONTROL; the CLIENT evaluates the frame function at its interpolated render tick; ALL subscribed shards share one integer celestial_tick. transfer_protocol: the SOURCE shard computes the destination `StampedPose` and ships it in FlushComplete (dest USES it, does not recompute); celestial body poses come from an orchestrator 'Ephemeris Authority' single-writer that shards CONSUME. identity_persistence: `FrameRef{kind,anchor_realm,valid_at_universe_ms}` travels with the pose and the RECEIVER re-evaluates at its own analytic clock; frames derived per-shard from a synced analytic clock, no central Ephemeris Authority. So: who computes celestial body positions (each shard from shared tick / orchestrator Ephemeris Authority / each shard from synced analytic clock) and who computes a transferred entity's dest-frame pose (client / source shard / receiving shard) are answered differently in each.
issues.resolution: Split into the two distinct questions and pick one answer each. (1) Celestial body ephemeris: adopt transfer_protocol's Ephemeris Authority as the single writer of body poses per tick (kills cross-binary brahe determinism risk for authority), BUT expose it as identity_persistence's closed-form `f(seed, universe_tick)` so clients and ghost-render can evaluate locally without a round-trip — the orchestrator value is authoritative for authority decisions, the closed-form is the deterministic fallback for rendering. Keep connection_plane's client-side `ReferenceFrameDef` evaluation as the CLIENT'S consumption of that same closed form (it never needs the orchestrator value). (2) Transferred-entity dest pose: transfer_protocol wins — the SOURCE computes the dest StampedPose authoritatively and ships it; the dest uses it and re-advances forward analytically (identity_persistence agrees). This removes the cross-binary recompute. Unify the three pose/frame structs (`ReferenceFrameDef`/`StampedPose`/`FrameRef`) into ONE `StampedPose{frame_ref, pos, vel, orient, universe_tick}` in shared core; `validity_range` from connection_plane is retained for late-frame application.

issues.issue: Whether a single global tick exists is contradicted. connection_plane asserts 'ALL subscribed shards share one celestial clock ... an integer tick counter advanced by the simulation, NOT read from each shard's wall clock' and binds every SnapshotFrame to one authoritative `celestial_tick` shared across shards. test_harness explicitly states the OPPOSITE: 'Production tick numbers are NOT globally synchronized ... Real shards are separate pods with independent tick loops ... every cross-shard message carries the sender's source_tick' and adds a 'staggered-stepping mode' precisely because ticks differ. transfer_protocol uses per-shard monotonic-disciplined Instant ticks. identity_persistence separates an orchestrator-authoritative 'analytic clock' (for celestial math) from per-shard local sim ticks that may lag. connection_plane's compositing invariant (evaluate all subs at 'the common render tick') assumes a shared tick that the other three deny exists.
issues.resolution: test_harness + identity_persistence + transfer_protocol win: there is NO globally-synchronized simulation tick; prod shards tick independently. connection_plane must change its compositing model: the shared quantity is the orchestrator-authoritative ANALYTIC universe time (identity_persistence's clock), an integer `universe_tick` that is closed-form and identical-by-construction (seed + integer epoch + elapsed), NOT a simulation tick advanced in lockstep. Snapshots carry the SENDER's `source_tick` (per transfer_protocol/test_harness) so the client/gateway can place each sub's entities in their own frame; the client composites by evaluating every frame function at the client's single render `universe_tick`, which is well-defined because frames are closed-form `f(universe_tick)` (resolves connection_plane's intent without requiring lockstep sim ticks). Rename connection_plane's 'celestial_tick' to 'universe_tick' and define it as the analytic clock value, not a sim tick. Adopt identity_persistence's durable monotonic clamp + write-ahead tick ceiling as the authority for this value.

issues.issue: Login/session identity crypto primitive conflicts directly. transfer_protocol mandates `SessionTicket = Ed25519-signed {player_id, entity_id, issued_epoch, expiry, nonce, conn_binding}` issued by the orchestrator auth service, and shards 're-verify on every transfer against the current ticket'. identity_persistence mandates `SessionTicket = HMAC-SHA256` day-1 (Ed25519/PASETO explicitly DEFERRED), validated ONLY by the gateway, and states 'Shards never see the ticket'. connection_plane assumes an Ed25519 `login_ticket` in `Hello` validated against an auth-service pubkey, plus a SEPARATE HMAC `ResumeTicket`. So: is the session credential Ed25519 or HMAC, and do shards verify it (transfer_protocol yes) or never see it (identity_persistence/connection_plane no)?
issues.resolution: identity_persistence wins on the primitive split and the shard-blindness; connection_plane wins on the login-vs-resume distinction. Unify to: (a) LOGIN credential = Ed25519 `login_ticket` presented once to the gateway (connection_plane), validated against the auth-service pubkey — this is the strong identity. (b) In-session SESSION ticket / resume = HMAC-signed by the gateway cluster key (identity_persistence + connection_plane ResumeTicket), gateway-only validation, single-use nonce. (c) Shards NEVER verify a client ticket (identity_persistence + connection_plane C2); they trust a `session_id` only over mTLS from the directory-current authority with a valid fence, AND only when the saga attested the session to that shard (connection_plane Section 3 AttachSession). transfer_protocol MUST drop 'shards re-verify the ticket on every transfer' and drop `entity_id` from the ticket (see EntityId-binding issue). Defer PASETO per identity_persistence staging.

issues.issue: EntityId is bound into the session credential by one design and absent in another. transfer_protocol embeds `entity_id` inside the Ed25519 `SessionTicket` and treats the entity as the moved thing with a distinct lifecycle. identity_persistence's `SessionTicket` (HMAC) contains `session_id, account_id, universe_epoch_id` but NO entity_id; its moved unit is the player keyed by session_id, and its directory keys are Entity/Region/Realm/session. connection_plane uses `PlayerId` + `SessionId` and never mentions EntityId. So the relationship player <-> session <-> entity and who mints EntityId is unspecified at the seam: transfer_protocol mints `EntityId(u128){kind,mint_shard,seq,rand}` on a shard, but identity_persistence's principal is `AccountId`/`session_id` minted by the orchestrator.
issues.resolution: transfer_protocol owns the EntityId concept (it is the authority-model's moved unit and needed for ghosts/visibility); keep `EntityId(u128){kind,mint_shard,seq,rand}`. identity_persistence owns the durable principal (`AccountId`) and the `session_id`. Resolve by: do NOT embed entity_id in the credential (a player may control multiple entities over a session — ship, EVA body); instead the directory holds the `session_id -> player_id -> {owned EntityIds}` mapping. The player's avatar EntityId is minted at first spawn by the spawning shard and recorded in the player checkpoint (identity_persistence's `player_ckpt`). All four designs must use the triple consistently: `AccountId` (durable principal), `session_id` (connection-session principal, cross-shard), `EntityId` (simulated thing). Remove `entity_id` from transfer_protocol's ticket; add the `session_id<->EntityId` directory mapping.

issues.issue: The transfer-lifecycle owner has four names and an unclear home. connection_plane: 'the Transfer Saga (owner, P7)', external to the gateway, consumed via a contract-tested seam. transfer_protocol: 'Transfer Coordinator' inside the ORCHESTRATOR (per-key-serial saga, redb WAL). identity_persistence: 'the orchestrator' running `vd-saga` (a pure FSM) as the single durable owner. test_harness: 'saga FSM' as a pure `fn step(State,Event)`. They agree on the SHAPE (pure FSM + durable wrapper) but connection_plane treats it as an opaque external service while the others place it concretely in the orchestrator, and only identity_persistence/test_harness specify the pure-function boundary.
issues.resolution: Merge to one named component: the Transfer Saga lives IN the orchestrator process (transfer_protocol + identity_persistence), implemented as a pure FSM crate `vd-saga` (identity_persistence + test_harness) wrapped by the orchestrator with redb persistence and at-least-once delivery. connection_plane's 'Transfer Saga seam' is this same component accessed over the gateway<->orchestrator control link; its contract-tested types (TransferControl command/ack set) are the public interface. Adopt connection_plane's exact command/ack vocabulary (PrepareSubscribe/RequestCut/FreezeSource/CommitAuthority/ThawSource/AbortTransfer/ReleaseSubscribe) as the gateway-facing API, and transfer_protocol's internal FSM (IDLE/PREPARE/FLUSH/FENCE_DEMOTE/PROMOTE/CLEANUP) as the orchestrator-internal states, with an explicit documented mapping between the two. One owner, one home, two named layers (external command API vs internal FSM).

issues.issue: Ghost physics behavior conflicts, and one variant risks violating the binding 'players must physically collide' standard. connection_plane: a Ghost slot is FROZEN — 'kinematic, NO independent physics integration ... advances ONLY by replaying authoritative pose deltas forwarded from the source ... a passive mirror, not a second simulation.' transfer_protocol: a Ghost 'collides, never integrates' and inserts a 'kinematic collider' so players on different shards physically collide across the band. These are reconcilable in intent (no independent integration) but connection_plane says the ghost advances only by forwarded source deltas during PREPARE, while transfer_protocol/identity_persistence rely on the ghost being a continuously-maintained kinematic collider during the whole overlap band (for cross-shard collision, Section 9), not only during a transfer's prepare window. If the ghost only exists/advances during a transfer prepare (connection_plane), two players merely co-located in an overlap band (no transfer) would NOT collide — violating the standard.
issues.resolution: transfer_protocol/identity_persistence win on scope: ghosts are continuously maintained for the WHOLE time an entity is in the overlap band (driven by the interest/band system), independent of any transfer, so cross-shard collision works for mere co-location (satisfies 'players must physically collide'). connection_plane wins on the integration rule: a ghost is a kinematic collider that NEVER independently integrates physics — it advances by source-forwarded pose deltas (GhostDelta datagrams). Reconcile: the ghost is always a kinematic collider fed by GhostDelta; 'frozen during transfer' (connection_plane) is just the special case where the source-owned entity is itself Frozen. connection_plane must extend ghost lifetime from 'prepare window' to 'full overlap-band membership'. The single shared ghost-delta transport (transfer_protocol Section 1.4 datagrams) carries these poses for both visibility and transfer; connection_plane's gateway-forwarded prepare-deltas and transfer_protocol's shard<->shard GhostDelta datagrams must be unified into ONE replication channel (see next issue).

issues.issue: Two ghost/snapshot replication transports that overlap. connection_plane routes ALL world state to the client through the gateway from shards via a gateway<->shard pool (BULK/EVENTS/SNAPSHOT), and ghost prepare-deltas are 'forwarded from the source via the gateway during prepare'. transfer_protocol defines a DIRECT shard<->shard GhostDelta datagram channel (plus a reliable control stream) for cross-shard ghosts/visibility, NOT via the gateway. So a cross-shard ghost pose travels shard->shard (transfer_protocol) for collision/visibility on the neighbor shard, but ALSO must reach the client, which per connection_plane is shard->gateway->client. The designs do not state how the shard<->shard ghost plane and the gateway snapshot plane compose, risking duplicate pose paths or a pose the neighbor shard has but the gateway never sends.
issues.resolution: Both planes are needed and are NOT duplicates once scoped: (1) shard<->shard GhostDelta (transfer_protocol) exists so a NEIGHBOR SHARD can run a kinematic collider and include the ghost in ITS authoritative snapshot. (2) The client receives that ghost as a normal entity inside the neighbor shard's snapshot via shard->gateway->client (connection_plane). Resolution: the ghost, once spawned on the neighbor shard, is just another entity in that shard's snapshot stream to the gateway — the client never receives a 'ghost' specially (matches transfer_protocol Section 9 'client never knows some entities are cross-shard'). Delete connection_plane's notion of the gateway separately forwarding 'prepare pose deltas'; during PREPARE the dest shard already has the ghost via shard<->shard GhostDelta and emits it in its snapshot. The gateway forwards snapshots only; it is never a ghost-pose router. Document the two planes (shard<->shard replication vs shard->gateway->client snapshot) as orthogonal in the integration spec.

issues.issue: Serializer decision conflicts. connection_plane mandates 'v1: postcard EVERYWHERE — CONTROL, INPUT, BULK, EVENTS, SNAPSHOT, gateway<->shard, saga' and explicitly argues AGAINST a second live codec ('maintaining two live codecs doubles the schema-evolution mental model'), reserving the bitcode flag bit for later. transfer_protocol mandates 'postcard for control/saga; bitcode for same-version 20Hz world snapshots / GhostDelta'. identity_persistence mandates 'postcard for control/saga/checkpoint; bitcode for same-version 20Hz world snapshots'. So two designs ship bitcode for snapshots in v1; connection_plane forbids it in v1.
issues.resolution: connection_plane wins for v1 (it owns the wire and makes the strongest argument: at dozens of players the bitcode size win is noise and two live codecs is a footgun that already bit this project as protocol-fb drift). v1 = postcard everywhere, with the codec flag bit reserved. transfer_protocol and identity_persistence must change their 'bitcode for snapshots/GhostDelta' to 'postcard v1, bitcode gated behind a profiler-proven bandwidth bottleneck via the reserved flag bit' — i.e. defer bitcode to a v1.1 change that does not break the wire. This keeps one schema-evolution model while preserving the upgrade path all three wanted.

issues.issue: Directory ownership-key space differs across designs. connection_plane's Directory answers 'who owns SESSION X' and stores resume_nonce/session_gen/transfer_in_progress per session. transfer_protocol's directory keys are `Entity(EntityId) | Region(RegionId) | Ship(ShipId)` with `in_transfer`. identity_persistence's directory keys include `session:<session_id>` (with gateway_gen) AND entity/realm ownership. So the directory is described as session-keyed (conn), entity/region/ship-keyed (transfer), and session+entity+realm-keyed (identity). Without one key model, the gateway's session-lease lookup and the saga's entity-ownership CAS hit different stores or different key conventions.
issues.resolution: identity_persistence's superset wins (it is the only one with both session AND entity/realm keys). Unify the directory key space to a single tagged key: `Session(session_id) | Entity(EntityId) | Realm(RealmId) | Ship(ShipId)` where RealmId subsumes Region (planet_seed/system_seed/ship_id). One OwnerRecord shape `{authority: ShardRef|GatewayRef, fence, lease_expires, in_transfer: Option<TransferId>}` for all key kinds (identity_persistence's record + transfer_protocol's in_transfer field, which transfer_protocol already made enforced). connection_plane's session-lease state (resume_nonce, transfer_in_progress) lives on the `Session` key. This makes session-failover (gateway_gen CAS) and entity-transfer (fence CAS) the same directory operation on different keys.

issues.issue: Duplicate durable per-shard idempotency-leg store under two names/keys. transfer_protocol: per-shard 'transfer_leg' WAL recording 'froze E for T at lease_epoch E' / 'accepted E for T at version N+1' before applying effects, keyed by (TransferId, version). identity_persistence: per-shard `applied_steps` table keyed by `(correlation_id, step_id)` written in the same txn as the side effect. test_harness: correlation-id tombstones `(cid -> terminal_state)` for idempotency. These are the same responsibility (durable, idempotent, per-side-effect record on each shard) with three key schemes: (TransferId,version) vs (correlation_id,step_id) vs (cid->terminal).
issues.resolution: identity_persistence's `applied_steps` keyed by `(correlation_id, step_id)` wins as the general mechanism (step_id is finer-grained than version and decouples idempotency from the directory version number). Rename transfer_protocol's 'transfer_leg' to be a SEMANTIC log layered ON `applied_steps` (the leg content 'froze/accepted' is the value; the key is (correlation_id, step_id)). Adopt test_harness's single-use-terminal tombstone as the saga-level complement (terminal cid blocks late duplicate PREPARE). Standardize: TransferId == correlation_id (one u128, see correlation-id issue). One table `applied_steps: (correlation_id, step_id) -> StepRecord` per shard, plus saga-terminal tombstones in the orchestrator.

issues.issue: Per-shard persistence keying conflict: shard_id vs RealmId. transfer_protocol describes 'per-shard WAL' and 'per-region/per-ship block-delta store'. identity_persistence is emphatic that stores are keyed by `RealmId` (planet_seed|ship_id|system_seed) on a persistent volume, NOT shard_id (citing the old `/tmp/...{shard_id}.redb` bug that lost edits on re-shard), with single-writer realm ownership in the directory. connection_plane is persistence-agnostic but its resume path reads 'the authoritative resume seq from the shard's durable checkpoint via the Directory' — implying a shard-addressed checkpoint. test_harness's Store is per-NODE (node==shard). If checkpoints/block-deltas are keyed by shard_id, a re-sharded planet loses state (the exact old bug).
issues.resolution: identity_persistence wins decisively (this is a re-verified old-system data-loss bug). All durable WORLD state (block_wal, chunk_snapshot, player_ckpt, config_state, grants, ship_design) is keyed by `RealmId` on a RealmId-addressed persistent volume; the directory's Realm key records which shard currently owns/opens that redb file (single-writer). transfer_protocol must change 'per-shard WAL' to 'per-realm WAL owned by the current realm-owner shard'. connection_plane's resume must read the checkpoint via the Directory's Realm-owner indirection, not a shard address. test_harness's Store stays per-node but the node's identity for store purposes is its owned RealmId set, not its NodeId. Block edits originating in a ghost/overlap region are FORWARDED to the realm owner (identity_persistence Section 5.1), never written locally — add this rule to transfer_protocol's ghost spec (ghosts carry no authoritative block edits, which it already states).

issues.issue: Timeout/deadline philosophy conflicts and partially violates the 'no magic numbers' standard. transfer_protocol uses FIXED timeouts (T_prov=30s, T_prep=2s, T_flush=1s, T_demote=1s, T_promote=2s, T_swap=2s, T_clean=5s). identity_persistence uses ADAPTIVE `adaptive_deadline = now + k*measured_RTT` plus an unconditional `hard_deadline`, explicitly 'NOT a magic constant'. connection_plane puts ALL operational constants in a single `TransportTuning` struct (gw_shard_control_timeout, resume_nonce_ttl, etc.) loaded from config. The user standard says no magic numbers but connection_plane amends it: transport/operational params live in one tunable struct. transfer_protocol's hard-coded seconds are exactly the magic numbers the standard and the other two designs reject.
issues.resolution: connection_plane + identity_persistence win. transfer_protocol's fixed T_* must become either (a) adaptive `k*measured_RTT` with a `hard_deadline` cap (identity_persistence) for the saga-internal deadlines, or (b) entries in a single tuning struct (connection_plane's TransportTuning) with documented derivation and startup-validated invariants, NEVER inline literals. Unify: saga phase deadlines = adaptive (k*RTT) with a hard cap; all the k, cap, grace, dwell, nonce_ttl, pool_size constants live in ONE config struct (merge connection_plane's `TransportTuning` and any saga-timing config into a single reviewed surface). Adopt connection_plane's amended standard interpretation explicitly (operational params are config, not seed-derived) across all four designs.

issues.issue: Source-ghost demote duration specified three incompatible ways, one of which re-introduces the banned magic number. transfer_protocol: source stays a ghost for `demote_after_ticks` (a count). identity_persistence: source converts to ghost for `demote_after_ticks` then despawns (a count). connection_plane: 'ReleaseSubscribe after demote grace' (a grace, in TransportTuning). test_harness: explicitly DELETES the magic `DEFAULT_SOURCE_DEMOTE_TICKS=15` and replaces it with LEASE-BASED demotion — 'source demotes its ghost ONLY upon a destination-acked ghost-delivered-to-all-observers signal, never a fixed count', asserting an inequality chain band > delay >= demote_latency.
issues.resolution: test_harness wins (it directly targets and deletes the banned magic 15 that all the others' 'demote_after_ticks' would re-introduce). Source ghost demotion is EVENT-driven, not count-driven: the source demotes/despawns its post-transfer ghost only when (a) the destination acks the entity is delivered to all observers AND (b) the entity has left the overlap band (so the ghost is no longer needed for collision/visibility). transfer_protocol and identity_persistence must replace `demote_after_ticks` with this lease/ack-driven condition. Any residual timeout is a safety cap in the config struct (not the primary mechanism), per the timeout-philosophy resolution. test_harness's inequality `overlap_band_ticks > max_fabric_delay >= demote_latency` becomes a CI-asserted invariant for the unified design.

issues.issue: Correlation-ID identity and naming drift: TxnId vs TransferId vs correlation_id vs idempotency_key. connection_plane uses `TxnId` for transfer correlation on every frame/span. transfer_protocol uses `TransferId` as the correlation ID AND a separate `idempotency_key=(TransferId,version)`. identity_persistence uses `correlation_id:u128` AND a separate `idempotency_key:u128` AND `step_id`. test_harness uses `TransferCorrelationId` / `CorrelationId` / `MsgId`. Four names for the cross-process transfer correlation token, plus two designs add a separate idempotency_key field whose relationship to the correlation id is defined differently.
issues.resolution: Standardize ONE u128 `TransferId` (== correlation_id == TxnId == TransferCorrelationId) generated by the orchestrator at saga creation, carried on every message/span/frame touching the transfer (P8). Per-step idempotency uses `(TransferId, step_id)` (identity_persistence's finer scheme) — DROP the separate opaque `idempotency_key:u128` field (it is redundant with TransferId once TransferId is unique-per-saga; transfer_protocol's `(TransferId,version)` collapses to `(TransferId, step_id)`). Rename all occurrences (TxnId, correlation_id, TransferCorrelationId) to `TransferId` in the unified vocabulary. test_harness's `MsgId` stays distinct (it is a per-message wire id for at-least-once dedup, not the transfer correlation).

issues.issue: Reconnect/adoption authority split between gateway and orchestrator is described with different mechanisms that must interlock but are specified independently. connection_plane: adoption is 'Directory-mediated eviction' where the adopting gateway CAS-bumps `session_gen`; if `transfer_in_progress=Some`, the gateway registers with the SAGA and the saga replays through it. identity_persistence: resume does a 'directory CAS bumps gateway_gen, owner->B; orchestrator PUSHES revoke to A; A self-fences'. test_harness: gateway crash -> client reconnects, new gateway rebuilds route from directory. These are the same flow but connection_plane drives the CAS from the gateway while identity_persistence has the orchestrator push the revoke; and connection_plane adds a saga-registration step on in-flight transfer that identity_persistence does not mention.
issues.resolution: Merge into one flow: the adopting gateway initiates the session-lease CAS (connection_plane) on the `Session` directory key, bumping the session fence; the orchestrator (directory owner) performs the CAS and pushes revocation to the old gateway, which self-fences (identity_persistence) — these are the same CAS viewed from two ends, not two mechanisms. Add connection_plane's in-flight-transfer rule universally: if the Session record has `transfer_in_progress=Some(TransferId)`, the orchestrator routes subsequent saga steps through the newly-adopted gateway (the saga is the sole recovery authority). Specify once in the unified spec under 'session failover', referencing the single fence CAS.

issues.issue: Spatial-precondition / ABORT path exists in transfer_protocol but connection_plane's saga command set lacks a typed spatial-reject ack, risking a gap at the seam. transfer_protocol has explicit `PrepareAck{spatial_ok:false} -> ABORT_SPATIAL` with typed `TransferRejected{reason}` (e.g. 'hatch obstructed') and a player staying on source. connection_plane's `PrepareSubscribe -> Prepared{ghost_ready}` ack carries only `ghost_ready` (a bool-ish readiness), with no spatial-precondition-failure variant; its abort path is generic `AbortTransfer`. So the gateway-facing command contract (connection_plane) cannot represent the dest's 'spatially impossible' rejection that transfer_protocol's saga depends on.
issues.resolution: transfer_protocol wins — spatial precondition failure is a real, user-visible abort cause ('hatch obstructed') that must be typed. connection_plane's `Prepared` ack must be widened to `PrepareResult { Prepared{ghost_ready} | Rejected{spatial_reason} }`, and the gateway must forward a `TransferRejected{reason}` cosmetic to the client (it already has `TransferCosmetic`). The saga's PREPARE -> ABORT_SPATIAL transition (transfer_protocol) maps to the saga issuing `AbortTransfer` after a `Rejected` ack. Add the spatial-reject variant to the contract-tested seam types (connection_plane Section 10).

issues.issue: Provisioning-aware (warp) transfer and on-demand shard creation is owned by transfer_protocol (AWAIT_PROVISION child saga, compensation, self-registration gating) and surfaced in test_harness (ProvisionIntent, persist-before-spawn, derived NodeId) and connection_plane (Spawn Resolver, [Failed] subscription retry/backoff), but the three do not agree on who computes the bootstrap interest and who gates the new pod. connection_plane: a stateless 'Spawn Resolver (provided by the saga/Directory seam)' computes initial InterestSet from the checkpoint. transfer_protocol: the Coordinator opens a provision child saga and the new pod self-registers only after asking 'am I still wanted for saga T?'. test_harness: orchestrator persists ProvisionIntent with NodeId=derive(cid,epoch) BEFORE spawn, spawn idempotent. These overlap on the same warp-provisioning responsibility without one named owner.
issues.resolution: transfer_protocol owns the provisioning saga (child saga + compensation + self-registration gating). test_harness's mechanism wins for the determinism detail: persist `ProvisionIntent{ provision_request_id, node_id=derive(TransferId, epoch) }` BEFORE spawn; spawn is idempotent; the new pod self-terminates if its saga is aborted (transfer_protocol's gate == test_harness's 'am I still wanted'). connection_plane's Spawn Resolver is the SEPARATE concern of computing the initial InterestSet once the dest exists — keep it, but clarify it runs AFTER provisioning completes (it needs a live dest to attach to) using the checkpoint position; it is provided by the orchestrator (the saga/Directory home), not a fourth component. One owner: orchestrator (provision child saga + Spawn Resolver), with test_harness's persist-before-spawn determinism rule.

issues.issue: Gateway<->shard transport vs the harness Node transport abstraction are not reconciled, risking the testability mandate failing at the integration boundary. connection_plane specifies a concrete gateway<->shard QUIC POOL (K connections per pair, SessionId+session_gen in-frame, mTLS, snapshot datagrams). test_harness specifies that ALL inter-node I/O goes through an injected `Transport` trait (enqueue-only send, drain_inbound, NodeUnreachable as async failure) so production code never calls quinn directly, and the gateway<->shard pool would be a `ProdIo` impl. transfer_protocol and identity_persistence describe their inter-shard transport (datagrams + reliable control stream; ACKed bidi streams) concretely without referencing the Transport trait seam. If the gateway and shards are written against concrete quinn pools (connection_plane) rather than the `Transport` trait (test_harness), they become the same bin-only-untestable artifacts the whole effort is trying to prevent (R5).
issues.resolution: test_harness's `Transport`/`ShardIo` trait seam is binding for ALL node code (it is the foundational testability contract and directly fixes R5). connection_plane's gateway<->shard pool, transfer_protocol's GhostDelta datagram channel, and identity_persistence's ACKed bidi envelope are all PROD implementations of the `Transport` trait (the `io-prod`/`ProdIo` crate), not parallel transport stacks. Mandate: the gateway and every shard are libraries built against `ShardIo`; the concrete quinn pool/datagram/stream choices live behind `Transport::send`/`drain_inbound`. connection_plane's enqueue-only backpressure and 'NodeUnreachable surfaces async' must match test_harness's exact `SendError::QueueFull` (sync) + `Inbound::NodeUnreachable` (async) contract. Add the `Transport` trait to connection_plane's seam list.

issues.issue: mTLS trust bootstrap conflicts on day-1 vs full. transfer_protocol mandates 'mTLS on all inter-process links' and per-shard cert SAN identity used for message authorization. identity_persistence explicitly DEFERS per-shard certs/CA/SPIFFE and ships day-1 with a STATIC shared cluster PSK cert (one cert both ends), cross-checking peer identity against the DIRECTORY (not the SAN). connection_plane mandates 'mTLS (cluster CA)' between gateway and shards. So transfer_protocol/connection_plane assume per-shard or CA-issued certs with SAN-based identity from day one, while identity_persistence ships a single shared cert and uses the directory (not the cert) as the identity source.
issues.resolution: identity_persistence wins on staging (its 6-8-weeks-of-infra-before-a-cube argument is decisive for a solo dev). Day-1: ONE static cluster cert (shared PSK) for mTLS on all inter-process links; peer authority identity is the directory-current owner + fence, NOT the cert SAN. transfer_protocol's 'SAN-based message authorization' and connection_plane's 'cluster CA' become a deferred hardening (per-shard ed25519 leaf certs + SPIFFE), gated on a real multi-tenant trust boundary. All three keep the property that no unauthenticated process can inject control messages (the static PSK gives that at dozens-of-players scale). Update connection_plane and transfer_protocol to 'static cluster cert day-1, CA/SAN deferred'.

issues.issue: Universe epoch / durable clock ownership and the COMMIT-derives-authority crash semantics are stated by multiple designs with subtly different recovery guarantees. identity_persistence: write-ahead-reserved tick ceiling, restart resumes at ceiling (never behind), monotonic clamp, epoch persisted at genesis, every record tagged universe_epoch_id+schema_version, mismatch -> discard/abort. transfer_protocol: universe epoch persisted, never regenerated from SystemTime, records tagged universe_epoch_id, leg whose epoch mismatches is discarded/aborted, plus 'on orchestrator restart ABORT all in-flight sagas to last-known owner' (Tier-3). connection_plane: 'persisted universe epoch' carried in Welcome/ResumeTicket, epoch mismatch re-mints the ticket. These mostly agree but transfer_protocol's Tier-3 'abort all in-flight sagas on orchestrator restart' conflicts with connection_plane's 'saga is sole recovery authority, replays remaining steps' and identity_persistence's 'recover directory + sagas, re-drive each saga to terminal honoring hard_deadline' (resume, not blanket-abort).
issues.resolution: identity_persistence + connection_plane win for the DURABILITY bar the user mandated ('durable transfer saga that survives orchestrator crashes mid-transfer'): on orchestrator restart, RESUME and re-drive sagas idempotently to terminal (DONE or ABORT), do not blanket-abort. transfer_protocol's 'Tier-3 abort-all' is acceptable ONLY as a temporary milestone-staging simplification (its own Section 3.2 frames it as such) and must be explicitly labeled a stopgap that the resume path (the actual requirement) replaces, NOT the target design. Adopt identity_persistence's write-ahead tick ceiling + monotonic clamp + epoch/schema tagging as the single clock/epoch authority; connection_plane consumes the epoch in Welcome/ResumeTicket and re-mints on rollover. One DurableUniverseClock owner: the orchestrator.

issues.issue: Hysteresis/overlap-band parameters are defined by two designs with different structure, and the velocity-scaling (critical for 110 km/s warp) exists in only one. connection_plane: interest uses `enter_radius > exit_radius` plus `min_dwell_ticks`, entity/seed-derived. transfer_protocol: a full per-class band TABLE (Planet SOI, System SOI, Ship hull, Sector edge, Warp) with VELOCITY-SCALED inner pad `max(3m, v_rel*dt*K_safety)`, swept-segment crossing detection, sustained-inward `N_entry` ticks, and `K_dwell` cooldown. connection_plane's simpler enter/exit radii lack the velocity scaling that transfer_protocol proves is mandatory (a 5.5 km/tick body tunnels a fixed band). These describe the same overlap-band/interest mechanism at different fidelity.
issues.resolution: transfer_protocol wins (velocity-scaled bands + swept-segment crossing are non-negotiable at orbital velocities; a fixed enter/exit radius is a tunneling bug). connection_plane's interest model must adopt transfer_protocol's per-class band table, velocity-scaled inner pad, swept-segment detection, sustained-inward entry, and dwell cooldown. connection_plane keeps ownership of the InterestSet DIFF protocol (add/remove to the gateway) and the chunk-cache; transfer_protocol owns the GEOMETRY that decides band membership. The two SOI functions (planet Hill-sphere vs system luminosity, confirmed distinct in core/src/system.rs:710 and core/src/galaxy.rs:217) must be the named, separately-tested `planet_soi`/`system_soi` per transfer_protocol, in shared core, used by the interest geometry.

issues.issue: Pervasive terminology drift for the same concepts beyond the fence/correlation-id issues already listed: 'subscription/SubscriptionId/sub_id' (connection_plane) vs 'interest set/ghost' (transfer_protocol) for what the client renders; 'authority/Owned/Ghost/Frozen' (transfer_protocol) vs 'authoritative sub / RouteSnapshot.authority' (connection_plane); 'shard' vs 'node' (test_harness uses NodeId generically for shard/gateway/orchestrator); 'realm' (identity_persistence) vs 'region/Region' (transfer_protocol) vs 'shard kind' (connection_plane); 'celestial_tick' vs 'epoch_tick' vs 'universe_ms' vs 'valid_at_universe_ms' vs 'source_tick' for time stamps on poses.
issues.resolution: Adopt one glossary in the integration spec: NODE (any process), SHARD (sim-authority node), REALM (RealmId = planet_seed|system_seed|ship_id; replaces Region), AUTHORITY state {Owned, Ghost, Frozen}, SUBSCRIPTION/sub_id (client-facing render layer), INTEREST SET (server-side membership driving subs and ghosts), FENCE (the one generation primitive), TransferId (the one correlation id), universe_tick (the one analytic clock value; replaces celestial_tick/epoch_tick), source_tick (per-shard local sim tick carried on messages). Map every design's local term to these once; this is mechanical but must be done before the contract-test crate freezes the shared types.

issues.issue: Crate/workspace layout proposals differ and would collide if taken literally. identity_persistence proposes vd-identity/vd-trust/vd-store/vd-fence/vd-time/vd-worldspec/vd-saga/shard-core + services. test_harness proposes sim/node/harness/tests (4 crates, io as a module, grow later). transfer_protocol proposes core/stub-shard/gateway/orchestrator + *-core libs. connection_plane proposes a `connection-plane` library crate + thin gateway bin. These are four different workspace skeletons for the same system.
issues.resolution: test_harness's 'start at 4 crates, grow on real pressure' philosophy wins as the meta-rule (avoids identity_persistence's 8-crate front-load). Reconcile concretely: shared types (fence, TransferId, StampedPose, directory records, saga FSM, clock) go in a `core`/`sim` lib (test_harness's `sim` == the pure domain + io traits as a module); `node`/`shard-core` is the one lib all shard kinds share (transfer_protocol + identity_persistence + test_harness agree on lib+thin-bin); `connection-plane` is a lib used by the gateway bin (connection_plane); the orchestrator hosts directory+saga+clock+auth. identity_persistence's vd-* split is the GROW-LATER target once second impls justify it, not the day-1 layout. Freeze the shared-types crate boundary first (it carries the contract-tested seam types) and let the rest follow test_harness's vertical-slice growth.

orphaned_responsibilities: INTERPOLATION-BUFFER OWNERSHIP & SIZE: All four designs assume the client interpolates on a 100-150ms buffer (no prediction), but NO design owns the buffer-vs-transfer-gap contract. connection_plane sizes the buffer; transfer_protocol's freeze gap and identity_persistence's sub-tick freeze window must both fit inside it; test_harness's POSE-CONTINUITY epsilon depends on it. Assign: connection_plane owns buffer size in TransportTuning; identity_persistence's 'freeze window < one tick' and transfer_protocol's InputGap bound must be asserted <= buffer headroom as a cross-cutting CI invariant. Currently no single owner guarantees freeze_gap + InputGap + stagger_skew < interp_buffer.

UNIVERSE-TICK ADVANCEMENT AUTHORITY: connection_plane assumes a shared celestial_tick 'advanced by the simulation' but never says WHICH process advances it; transfer_protocol has per-shard monotonic ticks; identity_persistence has the orchestrator DurableUniverseClock; test_harness says prod ticks are NOT synchronized. After resolving to one analytic universe_tick owned by the orchestrator, the responsibility 'who increments and publishes universe_tick, and how shards/clients obtain it without per-tick round-trips' is unassigned. Assign to orchestrator DurableUniverseClock published via a slew-synced analytic clock (identity_persistence), consumed closed-form locally.

EPHEMERIS AUTHORITY HOSTING & PUBLICATION RATE: transfer_protocol introduces an orchestrator-hosted 'Ephemeris Authority' that publishes body poses each tick, but connection_plane and identity_persistence have clients/shards compute celestial positions closed-form locally, and no design specifies the publication cadence, the wire family carrying ephemeris, or how it reconciles with local closed-form evaluation. Assign: orchestrator publishes authoritative body poses ONLY for authority decisions (spatial preconditions, dest-pose computation); rendering uses local closed-form f(seed,universe_tick). Needs a named message family and rate.

CROSS-SHARD BLOCK-EDIT FORWARDING: identity_persistence mandates that block edits in a ghost/overlap region are FORWARDED to the realm owner (single-writer redb), but neither connection_plane (which carries input) nor transfer_protocol (which carries ghosts) owns the path by which a player standing in an overlap band, whose input is routed to shard A, gets a block-edit applied to realm R owned by shard B. Assign: input action-frames for world mutation (the v1.1 reliable C->G actions) must be routed by the gateway/authoritative shard to the REALM owner, not the player's authority shard, when they differ. Currently no design routes block edits by realm-ownership.

REVOCATION FEED CONSUMER ON THE DATA PATH: identity_persistence defines the orchestrator pushing revoked session_ids/player_ids to gateway+shards, but the gateway hot path (connection_plane) is lock-free ArcSwap route reads with no described revocation check, and shards trust attested sessions. Who enforces a mid-session ban on the 20Hz input path, and with what latency, is unassigned. Assign: gateway checks revocation on CONTROL events + at resume, and on revocation tears the session down off the hot path; shards drop input on session-fence bump triggered by the revoke.

WARP MASKING VISUAL TRIGGER & SYNC: The user requires warp's 'system shrinks to a dot' masking visual; transfer_protocol streams ProvisionProgress{pct,eta} to stretch the visual, but the visual is a CLIENT render concern that connection_plane (client transport) only knows as a 'TransferCosmetic'. The mapping from saga AWAIT_PROVISION progress -> TransferCosmetic -> client warp-visual timeline is owned by no single design. Assign: orchestrator provision child saga emits progress -> gateway forwards as TransferCosmetic{warp_progress} -> client renders. Needs the cosmetic variant specified.

SHIP-INTERIOR vs SHIP-EXTERIOR AUTHORITY SPLIT AT THE CONNECTION LAYER: transfer_protocol Section 8 splits ship exterior authority (transfers between hosts) from interior (always ship-shard owned), and passengers are ChildOf(ShipId) re-parented atomically. But connection_plane's subscription model (the client composites 2-3 subs) and identity_persistence's RealmId (ship_id is a realm) do not specify how a player walking inside a flying ship is simultaneously subscribed to the ship-interior realm AND sees the exterior frame transform. The 'walk inside while flying' seam between the subscription/render-layer model and the versioned-bundle re-parent is unowned. Assign: ship interior = one subscription/render-layer in ShipLocal frame; exterior pose = the ship entity in the parent (system/planet) sub; client composites via frame nesting. Needs explicit specification of the nested-frame composition for the ship case.

CONTRACT-TEST SEAM TYPE OWNERSHIP: connection_plane mandates a single shared crate defining TransferControl/InterestSet/ownership-query/ResumeTicket with both-sided conformance tests, and test_harness mandates the saga FSM + io traits as shared types, but no design owns the MASTER shared-types crate that both the gateway, shards, orchestrator, and harness import. With four designs each defining overlapping types (OwnerRecord, Fence, TransferId, StampedPose) in their own vocabulary, the risk is the protocol-fb-drift failure recurring. Assign: a single `core`/`sim` crate owns ALL cross-process types and the contract-test conformance suite; freeze it before any subsystem implementation begins (this is the prerequisite the integration must enforce).
